issues.detail: The skill contains two near-duplicate Overview sections that repeat the same description of Payload, and the Instructions are dense bullets that cram many commands and options into single lines.

scenarios.name: local-api-visitor-access
scenarios.rationale: Both name the Local API default and the `overrideAccess: false` fix. A also passes `user` and says not to use `draft: true` on a public page, which matches the rubric closely. B passes `user` only in the editor example and leaves it out of the main fix, and it sets `draft: false`, which is slightly off the rubric's draft guidance but harmless.

scenarios.name: install-into-existing-nextjs-app
scenarios.rationale: Both list the correct packages, wrap next.config with withPayload, and give a buildConfig with secret, a Postgres adapter and lexicalEditor. B shows the full app/(payload) folder contents and the route-group restructuring, and also suggests copying the folder from a scratch create-payload-app project. A only says to copy the folder from the official template and hedges on details, and B's secret fallback of '' is a minor weakness.

scenarios.name: role-based-publish-workflow
scenarios.rationale: Both enable drafts, restrict the role field's update access to admins, and add a beforeChange hook that blocks publishing for non-reviewers; B defines both isAdmin and isStaff and its hook rejects any publish by a user without the right role, while A defines isAdmin and a role helper but its hook is skipped when req.user is absent, though A adds more caveats.
